key_concept: At equilibrium with $K = 1$, $\Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K = 0$, so $\Delta H^\circ = T\Delta S^\circ$ and $\Delta S^\circ = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{T}$ (with $T$ in kelvin).
steps: From $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ = 0$, we get $\Delta S^\circ = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{T}$.
Convert the temperature to kelvin: $T = 60 + 273 = 333\ K$.
Substitute: $\Delta S^\circ = \dfrac{666\ kJ\ mol^{-1}}{333\ K} = 2.0\ kJ\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}$.
why_not_others: Option (4), $11.1$, comes from dividing by $60$ (Celsius) instead of $333\ K$. Option (2), $2000$, is the correct value in $J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}$ but the question asks for $kJ$. Option (3), $333$, is just the temperature in kelvin.
common_trap: Using the temperature in °C ($60$) instead of kelvin ($333\ K$), or reporting the answer in $J$ when $kJ$ is asked.
time_saving_tip: Equal concentrations at equilibrium means $K = 1$ and $\Delta G^\circ = 0$, so directly compute $\Delta S^\circ = \Delta H^\circ / T = 666/333 = 2$.
